title: Dr. Bench: A Multidimensional Evaluation for Deep Research Agents, from Answers to Reports

live_model.evidence: Sec. 5.1: 'seven web-search-tool-enhanced reasoning models (gemini-2.5-pro, gpt-5-2025-08-07, ...)'; Table 1: 'GPT-5-2025-08-07 0.5560 0.4593 1.0383 27.3312 7006 0.0045'

prompt.location: Subject input is the benchmark query itself (example in Figure 9, 'Please write a report ...'); judge prompts in Appendix D
prompt.note: System prompt and web-search tool configuration for the subject models are not printed.

data.source: https://github.com/evigbyen/drbench/ (214 expert-validated queries with rubrics and annotations)

notes: Reports depend on live web search, so drift is expected; the SemanticDrift/TrustworthyBoost metrics need the benchmark's FAK/FDK and TSL annotation pipeline (Algorithm 1). o4-mini in live_ids is actually o4-mini-deep-research-2025-06-26, a different model. Temperature 0.

resolution.plan: Use the 214 queries, QSR rubrics, FAK/FDK/TSL annotations and the Algorithm 1 scoring code from the repository. Generate reports with gpt-5-2025-08-07 plus the web-search tool at temperature 0 (the subject-model system prompt and search configuration are not printed and must come from the repository); score Quality, SemanticDrift and TrustworthyBoost with the Appendix D judge prompts on gpt-4o-2024-11-20 and compare IntegratedScore with 27.3312 (Table 1).
resolution.approximation: Live web search makes reports time-dependent, so drift is expected; the subject-model prompt and search settings are the repository's.
